title: One-Hot to Binary Encoder
statement: Design a one-hot to binary encoder that converts an eight-bit one-hot input into a 3-bit binary output plus a valid signal. If the input is not one-hot or is all zeros, valid must be 0 and code must be 0. This module is useful in priority schemes and state decoders.
module_signature: module one_hot_to_binary(input [7:0] one_hot, output reg [2:0] code, output valid);
behavior: code reports the position of the asserted bit if exactly one input is high.
valid is 1 only if exactly one input bit is high.
If zero or multiple bits are asserted, valid is 0 and code is 0.
Purely combinational: outputs must settle after input changes.
Do not depend on initial register values, clocks, or delays.
All outputs must be driven to known 0/1 values for every input case.
constraints: Do not use sequential pipelines or internal state.
hint: Count the asserted signals and encode only when the count is one.
